design:face:1.name: Sight Lines: her face is her senses
design:face:1.pitch: Up close, the Matron is a real old woman's face under a white first-aid cap. Her skin is thin, with blue veins at the temples. A burn spreads across her right cheek, her lashes are thinning, and her nose bleeds and never quite stops. None of it is decoration, because her eyes are her sight lines. When her eyes find yours over the top of a crate, that is the moment she sees you. When they are turned toward some other noise, she really is not looking at you. While she has you, she stares without blinking until a tear runs. Then she blinks: the left lid comes down late and neither lid closes all the way, the whites roll up underneath, and for that third of a second you cannot be seen. After a chase she gasps with her mouth open and hears less. Then she goes still, holds her breath, and listens harder than ever. The bruise you gave her with a dropped toolbox is still on her left cheek an hour later.
mechanics: One owner for where she looks. A new native module, MatronFace (src/sim/matron_face.hpp/.cpp), is owned by Matron and stepped in Matron::pre_step at 90 Hz. Each tick it picks one thing for her to look at, from simulation facts only, in this order: the player's eyes if she saw him last tick; the loudest sound she picked this tick, after a delay that depends on her stage (0.30 s as a pest, 0.15 s dangerous, 0.08 s fully changed); her lead (heard_x_/z_, look_x_/z_); the next point on her route (target_x_/z_); and at her post, a fixed sweep across the cage mouth. Nothing in it is random. The view stops guessing: the yaw_to_player and _head_yaw lines in matron_view.gd are deleted.

Head on a neck. The head turns and tilts (yaw and pitch, relative to her body) as a two-axis spring-damper with a limited neck: head about 4.5 kg, inertia about 0.03 kg m^2, at most 10 N m of yaw torque, ±80 degrees. Stage sets how it moves: a pest turns slowly and smoothly, dangerous she turns fast, and fully changed the head overshoots and wobbles. In the Turn the limit opens to ±170 degrees, so the head facing the wrong way is real and she can then see behind her. Each eye turns on two axes up to ±45 degrees. Eyes jump to any target more than 2 degrees off, with real eye-jump timing (about 2.2 ms per degree plus 21 ms), and turn inward on close targets, which shows at half a meter.

Sight from her eyes to his eyes. sees() now casts from the simulation's eye point: her body plus a head offset for each posture (upright, stooped, all fours, climbing, clinging, peering), turned by her yaw and head angles. It keeps today's two rays kEyesHalfM apart. It casts to the player's eyes (new set_player_eyes(), which follows his crouch) and to his chest, so a single horizontal bar like ShaftRail cannot hide both. A ray only counts inside her field of view: within ±30 degrees she sees anyone; out to ±95 degrees she sees him only if he moves faster than 1.2 m/s or is within 2 m; with lids closed she sees nothing. The same gate covers sees_far_ (the 50 m catwalk commit). It works both ways: if you can see her eyes over cover, she can see yours.

Lids, blinks and tears, which decide whether she can see. Her eyes dry out until she has to blink: at rest about every 4 s. While she holds the player in sight they dry more slowly: half as fast as a pest, 0.3 times dangerous, 0.1 times fully changed, which gives stares of 8 to 40 s. Losing him sets off 2 or 3 blinks in a row. A blink lasts 0.3 s, and on the ticks both lids are closed (about 0.12 s) she sees nothing. Staring past 1.5 times the dryness that would make her blink wells up a tear in each eye (tear_s is exported, and the view runs it down the cheek at about 1.5 cm/s). Something moving at her head faster than 3 m/s from within 1.5 m makes her blink and flinch. That check is a sphere query around her head, sorted by BodyID so it stays deterministic. Exposure changes only how a blink looks: past 0.4 the left lid lags by 60 to 90 ms; past 0.75 the lids stop at 85% closed with the eyes rolled up. How long she is blind never changes, so her look follows exposure, what she does follows rage, and there is still no radiation gameplay.

Breath, which decides how well she hears. Effort from her own movement (hunt speed squared, climbing, the Turn, the cable) builds an oxygen debt that she pays back at rest over about 12 s. Debt and stage set how fast and deep she breathes. When Peering, or Guarding after a far noise (look_s_ > 0), she holds her breath for at most 25 s × (1 − debt), and ends with a gasp. Fully changed, her breathing swells and fades with 6 to 15 s stops (the breathing pattern of the dying). Her own breathing covers quiet sounds: her hearing reach is multiplied by a factor that is 1.0 at resting breath, about 0.75 when panting, and about 1.2 while she holds her breath or between breaths. At rest nothing changes from today. Each inhale, exhale and gasp is exported, so her breath sounds play in time with her chest and mouth.

Marks from what happened to her. These are looks only, but the simulation owns them and the checkpoint saves them. Twelve body areas build up wear from quantities the simulation already has: meters on all fours (palms, knees), meters climbed (palms), cable friction work, kCableFriction × kMassKg × g × across × |speed| × dt (raw forearms), vaults and leaps, hard landings (knees, chin), and hits to the head. A hit is an ImpactLedger hit within 0.35 m of her head point; its direction in the head's frame says which cheek, the brow, scalp or nose, and its energy sets how bad the mark is. The time of the last hit is kept per face area, so a bruise turns from red to purple over minutes. A hit on the nose starts a nosebleed, and past exposure 0.7 it does not stop.

Hitting her face really does something. A hit to the head kicks the neck by the piece's momentum (the speed change is the square root of 2E/m). Her head snaps aside, her gaze is knocked off the player and she blinks: she loses sight of him for about 0.3 to 0.6 s and is never hurt badly. That gives the owner's 'keep her at bay without killing her' a real move: drop something on her from the deck above, or swing a carried load into her.

Exposure on her face, as looks only, driven by view_.exposure on the existing 600 s clock. The stages follow real radiation injury, in order: pale skin and redness, dry then wet peeling skin (a wet shine), hair falling out (each hair card has its own threshold, and clumps fall when her head's turning jerks hard), bloodshot eyes, pinpoint bleeds under the skin, bleeding gums (seen when she pants), grey-violet dead skin at the center of the burn, and milky lenses that dull the highlight in her eyes. The burn is placed by an inverse-square falloff from fixed points where she handled the source (her right palm, her right hip pocket, the right side of her face), as in real lost-source accidents, so it fades the way a real burn does.

Small movements, drawn by the view from simulation inputs and timed on simulation time so they repeat exactly. A shake of 8 to 12 Hz (stronger with exposure and with oxygen debt). Chest, shoulders, nostrils and lips move with the simulation's breath phase and depth. Tiny eye jitter, which stops during a stare. During a held breath or a stop in her breathing, every sway goes still and only the shake is left. The attendant's habit: if she sees the player hurt (arm_broken) within 3 m, she gives a one-sided reassuring smile on the unburned side that never reaches her eyes.

The head, built in this container from free (CC0) assets. Start from the MakeHuman base mesh and shape targets, reachable over git: an old woman, aged further, with uneven sides, shaped in numpy. Then headless Blender 4.2 LTS (download.blender.org is reachable) subdivides it, sculpts it procedurally (fold lines, pores, sagging), and bakes normal, ambient occlusion, curvature and thickness maps onto a head of about 10k triangles. numpy then builds the skin color from melanin and blood maps, with blue vein paths at the temples, eyelids and neck, and age spots. The colors are checked against reference portraits made with Qwen-Image (Apache-2.0) through the Hugging Face connector. Also built: a roughness map, a condition texture (burn growth thresholds, pinpoint bleeds, blister normals) and area IDs in vertex colors. The export is a GLB whose blend shapes are named after the simulation's channels (eye-left/right-closure, nose-left/right-dilatation, mouth-open, mouth-compression, mouth-corner-puller, eyebrows inner-up, neck-platysma), with separate high-detail eyes, teeth, tongue, lashes and hair cards. TRELLIS (reachable) and Hunyuan3D-2 (404 through the connector) are not used: their meshes have no separate lids or blend shapes for the simulation to drive.

Rendering on Godot's Compatibility renderer, which has no subsurface scattering, no screen-space ambient occlusion, and draws every extra light as another pass. The skin shader fakes the soft look of skin with a lookup texture keyed to curvature, a blurred normal for diffuse light, two specular lobes, and light shining through thin parts (ears and nostrils glow when lit from behind), with the condition layers on top. The eye shader has a parallax iris, a dark ring around the iris, a pupil that widens when sees_player is true and stays wide late in the day, a wet edge along the lower lid, and veins in the whites. Tear strips are revealed by tear_s, and a strand of saliva stretches between her lips when her jaw opens wide. The full head is shown within 8 m, a lighter version within 25 m, and today's primitive head beyond that. The _eye_light omni light is removed. Budget for the full head: at most 8 draw calls, at most 25k vertices, and four 1024² ASTC 6x6 maps (about 2 MB).

Lighting reveals stay honest. Light changes how she looks (highlights in her eyes, light through her ears, her pupils), but never what she sees, because lamps are not objects in the simulation. The simulation turns her face into or out of the light (the work bulb at her post), and the light does the reveal.

Owner rules this design follows: 00_START_HERE.md rows dated 2026-10-19 night (a realistic, uncanny, adult-scary face; the player is never helpless and needs a way to keep her at bay that does not kill her). 03_EXECUTION/ACTIVE_GOAL_PROGRESS.md: 'her look follows the exposure; what she does follows her rage', and 'No radiation gameplay'. Governing laws 15, 22 and 26 (randomness may not decide consequential facts; one owner per fact; the presentation may not be a second simulation authority).

milestones.title: Her eyes are her sight
milestones.what: MatronFace with the head on a neck, eyes and the look-at choice. sees() and sees_far_ cast from the simulation's eye point to the player's eyes and chest, limited to her field of view. set_player_eyes() comes from PhysicsWorld and follows his crouch. The new state is added to the snapshot and bridge (head, gaze, eye_point, eyes, attend).
milestones.proof: A new native group, SCRAPERX_ONLY=matron-face. A player standing still 4 m directly behind a guarding Matron stays unseen for 5 s. Walking at her side at 1.5 m/s, he is seen; standing still there, he is not. Crouched behind a 1.0 m crate with his eyes below its top, he is unseen; standing, he is seen. On a hunt, every tick she sees him, her gaze point is within 0.3 m of his eyes. Groups matron, matron-collision, matron-mischief and determinism pass, and the full suite runs once because the snapshot layout changes.

milestones.title: Lids, tears and breath
milestones.what: Dryness-driven blinks: held back during a stare, a burst on losing him, closed lids blind her, plus tears and the flinch blink. The oxygen-debt breath model with breath-holds, fully-changed breathing stops, the breath factor on her hearing, and exported breath events.
milestones.proof: matron-face cases. Kept in sight for 20 s at 5 m, she blinks at most twice and a tear appears; once he is out of sight, at least 2 blinks within 2 s. On every tick both lids are at least 95% closed, sees_player is false, and it comes back when they open. After a 10 s full-speed hunt, a walking noise at the distance she hears at rest goes unheard; after 30 s quiet while Peering, a creep at 1.15 times her resting reach is heard. A fully changed Matron shows breathing stops of 6 s or more. Determinism is bit-for-bit.

milestones.title: What happened to her shows
milestones.what: Twelve wear areas built from all-fours meters, climbing, cable friction work, vaults, leaps and landings. Head hits from the ImpactLedger near her head point kick the neck and knock her gaze off. Bruise ages and the nosebleed. Wear and bruise ages are saved in Matron::Saved.
milestones.proof: An 18 kg toolbox dropped from 3 m onto her head point: her head turns faster than 3 rad/s, sees_player is false for at least 0.25 s, wear on the struck side rises, and she lives. One cable slide gives forearm wear within 5% of the friction work worked out from kCableFriction. 50 m on all fours raises wear on her palms and knees. A checkpoint restore brings back wear and bruise ages exactly; the save group passes.

milestones.title: The head asset
milestones.what: tools/face/ scripts: MakeHuman CC0 base (old woman, aged, uneven sides) shaped in numpy, then a headless Blender 4.2 sculpt and bake, then numpy skin color, roughness, condition texture and area IDs, then a GLB with blend shapes named after the simulation channels, plus eyes, teeth, tongue, lashes and hair cards. Outputs go in godot/presentation/life/face/, with the MakeHuman commit (a8bc2d5) and the CC0 license recorded.
milestones.proof: A clean rebuild from the scripts reproduces the committed outputs (a hash list). Godot 4.7 imports them headless with no errors. A turntable of the bare head at 0.6 m, in day and night light, rendered under Xvfb with gl_compatibility, is reviewed next to the Qwen-Image reference portraits.

milestones.title: The face drawn from the simulation
milestones.what: matron_view.gd swaps in the new head within 8 m and drives head, eyes, lids, breath, tears, wear and exposure from get_matron_state(). The skin and eye shaders work on the Compatibility renderer. The view's guesses about the player's position are removed, the small movements and the held-breath stillness are added, and _eye_light is removed.
milestones.proof: look_matron_gallery gets new face poses (mid-blink, eyes rolled up at exposure 1, a tear, winded, holding breath, struck, exposure 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1, day and night), captured under Xvfb. A new scenario, look_matron_eyes, checks for every posture that the drawn eye center is within 0.12 m of the simulation's eye_point and the drawn gaze passes within 0.1 m of its gaze point. grep shows no head or eye code in matron_view.gd driven by player_position.

milestones.title: Meeting her face by touch
milestones.what: touch_matron_act (ui_test_act.gd) meets her face in live play at each stage. While she sees him her eyes are on the camera; touch-only, he carries a piece to the edge above her and LET GO knocks her gaze off him.

Whenever sees_player is true her gaze is within 0.3 m of the camera, the dropped piece leaves sees_player false for at least 0.25 s and leaves a mark, and --capture writes a live eye-contact frame for each stage.

milestones.title: Fits the phone
milestones.what: LOD switches at 8 m and 25 m, alpha-scissor hair instead of blended hair, compressed maps, and no extra light passes from her.
milestones.proof: A look_matron_budget scenario reads Godot's Performance monitors with her face filling the screen: her full head adds at most 8 draw calls and at most 25k vertices, and the LODs switch at the set distances. An Android APK from CI played on the Galaxy Z Fold 6 holds its frame rate in the eye-contact scene. The container cannot measure the phone's GPU, so the owner's device confirms this one.

risks: The chase changes. A limited field of view, sight from her eyes, blinks and the breath factor on her hearing change how she hunts. Tests in /home/user/ScraperX/tests/sim_tests_matron.cpp and the touch playthrough of her first act may need retuning. The Saved and snapshot layout changes, so the full native suite (about 25 min) has to run once.

Her capsule does not match her drawn pose. The capsule is always upright and 2.1 m tall, while on all fours her drawn head is about 0.95 m up. Head-hit areas and her eye point come from per-posture offsets, checked against the drawing by a test, not from the true body shape. Something landing on the empty top of the capsule counts as a hit on her back.

The Compatibility renderer has no subsurface scattering or screen-space ambient occlusion, so the skin can look like wax. Realism rests on the lookup texture, light through thin parts, good maps and uneven sides, plus review against reference portraits and more passes if needed.
Phone performance cannot be measured here. Each light near her face adds a full pass in this renderer, so the draw-call and vertex budgets are proxies until the Fold 6 confirms them.
The asset tools are not in CI. Blender 4.2 is about 350 MB, and CPU bakes on 4 cores are slow. Outputs are committed with scripts that rebuild them, and can drift if the tools change.
The MakeHuman head is only moderately detailed and the old-age shapes look generic. Sculpt detail, uneven sides and the skin maps have to carry the realism.
Uncanny is a matter of taste. The owner must review frames. The marks (bruises, abrasions, a nosebleed) are kept subtle, as the brief asks: not gore for its own sake.

Her voice. Her breath and shriek are synthesized today (sound_bank.gd _matron_breath, _matron_shriek), but the owner's rule is that voices are recorded people. The simulation's breath events give the timing; recorded human breath, gasp and 'shh' clips still have to be found or recorded.

Determinism across ARM and x86 is still unproven, and the new oscillators add more floating-point state. They use only dt-integrated simulation state and the same std:: math, and are covered by the determinism group.

Owner rules may be read more strictly. Blink and breath timing follow stage (rage), never exposure, to respect 'no radiation gameplay'. Hitting her face to knock her gaze off answers only part of 'keep her at bay'. Lamps that dazzle her would need lamps in the simulation, which this design does not add.
design:face:1.wow: You lean out from behind a column at dusk. A meter and a half away she stands completely still, not breathing. A single tear runs down her burned right cheek because she has not blinked since she lost you, and her eyes are already on yours. It is not a camera trick: the moment you saw her eyes, her sight lines reached you. Then her lids come down, the left one late and neither all the way, the whites rolling up underneath. For that third of a second you cannot be seen, and you run.

design:face:2.name: The Kind Face: the Matron's face up close, built for the gasp
design:face:2.pitch: For most of the climb she is only a shape that shuffles, and up close she is a tired old site nurse with a white cap, thin grey hair pinned up and a kind, closed-mouth smile. Her eyes are wet and they look at you the way a real person does, flicking from your left eye to your right and back. Her head shakes a little, the way old people's heads do. Then she goes still: no breath, no shake, no blink, two or three seconds while your thumb hovers over the stick, until one eyelid comes down a beat behind the other and you hear her swallow. Over the climb the lost X-ray source works on one side of her face, in the order real radiation burns follow: redness, a blood-red patch in one eye, wet peeling skin, hair coming out in clumps. Her face also shows her stage, and the first time she fully catches you the camera does not shake. It holds still, her face 28 cm from yours, smiling, her eyes moving between your eyes. One of them stops coming back.
mechanics: PIPELINE (offline, run from this container, outputs committed, like src/voice/generate_fall_voice.py): a new tools/face/build_matron_head.py, run with python3 -I, does the following. (1) It fetches pinned MakeHuman CC0 assets from raw.githubusercontent.com at a fixed commit, each checked against a SHA-256: base.obj (hm08), targets/macrodetails/caucasian-female-old.target, the face modeling targets that give her current silhouette (hollow cheeks, hooked nose, pointed chin: the cheek/, nose/ and chin/ target folders, the same intent as matron_body.gd's FEATURES), the expression-unit targets under targets/expression/units/caucasian/ (eye closure L/R, mouth open, lip part, smile L/R, nostril flare L/R, brow), and eyes/high-poly/high-poly.obj. (2) It cuts the head off at the collar (measured: 9,096 triangles, 4,580 vertices), keeps MakeHuman's UVs, scales decimeters to meters and fits it to the `centre` pivot (+z forward, as in Body.head()). (3) It writes the blend shapes from the expression targets, plus custom ones: lid_follow_up and lid_follow_down, burn_sink (the dead center of the burn sinks 2 mm) and denture_drop. (4) For fine detail it runs Blender 4.2 LTS headless (the tarball is reachable, pinned and cached outside the repo): two levels of subdivision, displacement from code-made wrinkle and pore fields (forehead lines, crow's feet, smile lines, vertical lines round the lips, neck rings, cell-noise pores), then a bake to the low mesh: a 2048 tangent-space normal map, curvature into vertex color R and thickness into vertex color G. Fallback: an exact numpy bake, which works because the high mesh is the low mesh displaced. (5) A 2048 albedo made in numpy in UV space, in layers: melanin base, red zones (nose, cheeks, ears, lip and eyelid rims), blue zones (under the eyes, temples), age spots from seeded Poisson disks. No photo is used, so the licences note can stay true. (6) A 1024 mask texture: R = burn field, G = blister and spot speckle (a threshold per texel, so one exposure number grows them in order), B = vein network grown in UV space from the temples, eyelids and neck, A = the order the hair falls out. (7) The skin_lut.png pre-integrated skin table (Penner, from d'Eon's six-Gaussian skin profile; the generator is already written and rendered in this container). (8) A GLB export with shape keys to godot/presentation/life/matron_face/, imported with the project's existing ETC2/ASTC compression.

OPTIONS CHECKED AND NOT USED: the Hugging Face connector's space list has no 3D generator. tencent/Hunyuan3D-2 returns 404. trellis-community/TRELLIS is reachable, but it gives one fused mesh with lighting baked into the texture, no separate eyeballs, eyelids or mouth inside, and no shape that can blink or open its jaw. The eyes and mouth are where the fear lives. No CC0 head scan exists on the allowed hosts: Poly Haven has no people and threedscans.com has statues. MakeHuman's base comes from scans, is CC0, can be animated, has UVs, and on its own already looks like a real old woman (rendered flat-shaded here).

THE HEAD IN THE GAME: a new godot/presentation/life/matron_face.gd is built by matron_view.gd's _build_figure. It replaces lines 568-613 (the sculpted skull and jaw, the mouth_dark blob, the 18 teeth blobs, the eyeballs with the amber emissive `eye_glow` irises (ffc04a at 2.2, the Halloween look), the eye bags, ears, ribbon hair and scarf) under the same `centre` pivot. The poses stay as they are: _pose's jaw_open drives a jaw_open blend shape instead of turning the jaw mesh. The face's update(data, delta, camera_position) aims her eyes at the camera, which _update_figure already receives, not at the body (_pose now aims at player_position, about 0.6 m below the eyes).

SKIN SHADER (matron_skin.gdshader, GL Compatibility, so there is no screen-space SSS): a custom light() samples the pre-integrated table by N·L and the baked curvature, giving soft red falloff into shadow. A back-scatter term uses the baked thickness, so ears, nostril rims and eyelids glow red when a lamp is behind her. Roughness shows wetness: lips, eyelid rims and the burn once it weeps. Veins (mask B) show more as the exposure grows and when she is back-lit. The same material goes on her forearms and hands, using an object-space burn on the right hand, so the real head does not sit on clay arms. Proven here: a probe project rendered this light() with a varying passed from fragment to light, and the table, under gl_compatibility, with no shader errors and back-lit ears. Curvature from fwidth() left grey creases, so curvature is baked.

EXPOSURE ON HER FACE (extends _apply_exposure, keeps SKIN_FRESH > BLISTERED > GREY), in the order of a real lost-radiography-source accident. She picked the source up in her right hand and carried it in her right breast pocket, so the damage is one-sided. Exposure 0 to 0.2: a pale, tired kind face. 0.2 to 0.45: redness on the right cheek, temple and neck, cracked lips, and a red patch on the white of the right eye. 0.45 to 0.7: the burn weeps and shines, blisters glow when back-lit, small blood spots on the cheeks, a red line at the gums, hair thinning at the right temple. 0.7 to 1.0: the burn's center turns violet-grey, matte and sunken (burn_sink), with peeling at its edge, the right brow and lashes gone, the right iris milky, the veins plain, the skin grey. Nothing is gored: no exposed tissue, no dripping blood.

EYES (matron_eye.gdshader, MakeHuman's high-poly eye split into an eyeball and a cornea shell): the iris is drawn with parallax so it sits behind the cornea. The cornea has roughness 0.02 so it carries catchlights. An old person's grey ring around the iris. A thin wet tear line along each lower lid. The sclera reddens with exposure, plus the bleed mask on the right eye. Each eye aims at the camera on its own, so at 30 cm the eyes visibly converge. Saccades scan your face in a triangle (your left eye, your right eye, your mouth, every 0.3 to 0.6 s), as a person looking at a face does. The lids follow the eyes (the upper lid rises when she looks up). Blinks: normal is 15 a minute at 150 ms. Wrong blinks are seeded with the existing _hash so captures repeat: one lid 90 ms behind the other, a slow close and a snap open, and on the burned side a lid that does not fully come back up. Pupils get wider with stage.

HER STAGE IN HER FACE (the native's `stage`, which the player is never told). Pest: the kind closed smile, which never reaches her eyes (no crinkle at the corners). Eyes scanning, lids following, a 5 Hz head tremor of 0.25°, 14 breaths a minute. Dangerous: the smile drops, the mouth hangs open 4 mm. The lids stop following, so white shows above the iris. Wide pupils, flaring nostrils, fewer blinks. Changed: no blinks and no saccades. The left eye locks on you while the right drifts 6° outward. The jaw hangs, and the upper denture plate (too white, too even, against her own brown lower teeth) drops 3 to 5 mm from the gum. Breathing follows the real dying pattern: five gasps getting deeper, then 5 to 7 s of nothing.

TOO STILL (presentation only, seeded): when she sees you within 6 m and has stopped (speed < 0.3), after 0.4 s she freezes for 1.8 to 3.5 s: no tremor, no breath, no saccades, no blinks, and the matron_breath cue (the _breath_in timer in _update_figure) is muted. She comes out of it with a late-lidded blink, a recorded swallow and a long out-breath. An old person who never stops moving, then stops, reads as wrong at once. STATE_PEERING's held breath already points this way.

WHERE YOU LOOK (touch drag-look is the attention; no new controls): when her face is within 8° of the screen center she is composed (smiling as a pest, mouth closed even when dangerous). When she is within 5 m and her face is more than 20° off center, her jaw sags, her head rolls 12° and one side of the smile falls. Swing the view back and she snaps composed within three frames (the existing _stutter feel). On a phone held at arm's length the whole screen is in view, so players catch the change at the edge and are never sure.

MOUTH AND HAIR: lips are dry, lined and cracked at the burned corner, with a wet inner edge. A thin strand of saliva stretches between the lips past jaw_open 0.3 and breaks at 0.6 with a recorded tacky sound. As a pest, her tongue wets her lips every 8 to 14 s. Teeth are code-made: her own uneven lower teeth plus the denture plate. Hair is about 120 alpha-scissor cards (alpha-to-coverage when MSAA is on) from a strand atlas drawn by code, pinned into a thin bun under the white cap, with a few strands loose across the face. Cards switch off in mask-A order as exposure grows. In the Turn's wind-up (turn==1) a clump comes loose, falls and stays on the deck (a pool of 12), so you find grey hair on a rail before you see her.

LIGHT THAT SHOWS HER: (1) The burst: _tear_door no longer sets _work_light to 0. The caged bulb is knocked loose and swings on its cord (1.4 s period, dying out over 8 s), so her face is lit, dark, lit, a little closer on each swing. (2) _eye_light becomes a catchlight that lights only her corneas: a dim OmniLight whose light_cull_mask is a new render-layer bit carried only by her cornea meshes (the same cull-mask technique main.gd uses with BATCH_FAR_LAYER). In the dark you see two small wet glints at head height, not glowing eyes. (3) Under the StackLamps (main_world.gd, 3.2 energy, 16 m range, on odd levels) the overhead light leaves her eye sockets black until she tilts her face up toward the camera. (4) On a ladder (head_pitch -1.1) her upturned face is lit from above by the deck you are standing on.

THE CATCH, second by second (only when the native counts a catch: `catches` rises in get_matron_state in the same tick as leave_corpse). 0 to 0.12 s: the camera is pulled 0.25 m toward her face with no shake, the world audio ducks 18 dB, and her face fills about 60% of the Fold's frame height. 0.12 to 0.9 s: stillness. No haptic. Her eyes converge on the lens and scan your eyes twice. The smile closes. One blink with the right lid late. A wet lip-part, close and dry: those 2 to 6 kHz mouth sounds carry on a phone speaker where low drones die. Then the right eye drifts off. At 0.9 s the existing pull-out over the corpse takes over (_ride_death), showing her standing over the body with her head cocked. _haptic(&"death") moves to this cut, and the break pulses follow. Reduced motion skips the pull but keeps the hold. After the second catch in a session the hold drops to 0.45 s, so the first is the gasp and later ones stay quick.

THE SHOVE (pest and dangerous): when the shove cue fires (`_shoves_seen` rises), her face is held close for 5 frames, still smiling, with a short recorded out-breath, then the native's shove throws you.

SOUND AND TOUCH: her breath, swallow, lip smack, tongue click and humming are recordings of real people. The sources are CC0 clips from Freesound (search is reachable and previews are on cdn.freesound.org; the API needs a key) or, if none fit, 8 short takes the owner records on the phone. These replace sound_bank.gd's synthesized _matron_breath. An offline loudness envelope per clip drives the lips and jaw, so what you see and hear match. A new haptic &"heart" [16 ms, 0.3], a two-beat pulse, runs while she sees you within 4 m, quickening from 70 to 120 bpm with nearness. It keeps going through her freeze and stops completely in the catch's hold. That missing beat is the cue.

risks: Accidental cheapness instead of planned wrongness: a CG face that looks like a mannequin reads as cheap, not frightening. Most of the realism must come from motion (saccades, breath, tremor, lids that follow), which the container can build exactly, more than from texture, which has no artist. The procedural albedo may look painted; layered skin and real anatomy reduce that but do not remove it.

Compatibility renderer limits: no screen-space SSS, SSAO or SSR. The probe proved custom light(), fragment-to-light varyings and the pre-integrated table compile and render. It also showed curvature from fwidth() makes crease artifacts, so curvature and thickness must be baked into vertex colors. Cornea catchlights depend on cull-mask support and the per-object light limit (8 by default).

Asset access: GitHub's API is blocked (403) for repos not attached to the session, so MakeHuman files must be fetched by known raw paths. Some guessed proxy paths (teeth, eyebrow, eyelash proxies, skin textures) returned 404, so teeth, lashes and textures are made by code. Another session in the shared scratchpad already has a sparse clone (scratchpad/mh) working, which could be reused. The Blender download is 352 MB, and the bake runs on 4 CPU cores; there is a numpy fallback.

The voice rule: today's matron_breath and matron_shriek are synthesized (sound_bank.gd). Syncing the face needs recorded human clips. Whether CC0 recordings of an old woman breathing and swallowing exist at good enough quality is unknown; the fallback is the owner recording 8 takes on the phone, which blocks milestone 4's audio.
The real head sits on a body of primitives (lofted arms, hooked fingers). The skin shader on the hands and arms narrows the gap, but the body may need its own pass later.
The death hold adds 0.9 s to a death. Repeated catches could drag, which is why the hold shortens after the second. The camera pull could cause motion sickness; reduced motion skips it.

Tone: radiation injuries could tip into gore. The art bible is limited to documented clinical signs (redness, wet peeling, blood spots, eye bleeding, hair loss, a necrotic patch), with no exposed tissue and no dripping blood.

Phone legibility: beyond about 4 m her face is under about 60 px on the Fold, so most of this only lands up close. The design deliberately puts its reveals at the burst, under the lamps, on the ladder, the shove and the catch. If players rarely get close, the work is wasted.
Performance on the device is unproven: 2160x1856 at render_scale 1.0 on HIGH, with the face filling the screen for 0.9 s. There is no Fold run (the release plan's device baseline is still open).
Merge risk: the working tree changed under me during this read (ui_test_chase.gd modified, a new commit 554357b), so another session is active on the same Matron files.
design:face:2.wow: She is fully changed and her hands close on you. The world goes quiet and the camera does not shake. Her kind, real face is 28 cm from yours, still smiling, the cheek on one side red and wet. Her eyes move from your left eye to your right eye and back, the way anyone looks at a face. She blinks, one lid a beat behind the other, and the right eye does not come back to you. Only then do you feel the phone thump in your hand as the view pulls out over your own body, and she is standing over it.

design:face:3.name: The Pupil Check: her real face, built from CC0 human scan topology
design:face:3.pitch: From across the deck she looks like a tired old first-aid attendant in a white cap. Closer in, she looks real enough that the small things start to bother you. Her wet eyes follow you while her head lolls. She stops blinking the moment she sees you, and every bit of her goes still. When she does blink, one eye closes a beat after the other. The burn has a story in its shape: it starts at her left breast pocket, where she carried the lost radiography source, and over the run it climbs her neck, from redness to peeling skin to a shiny weeping patch. Veins show through the skin, small dark-red spots come up, her hair comes out in patches, one eye clouds over and one pupil stays wider than the other. When her hands finally kill you, the camera stays in your dead eyes. She leans in with a polite, professional smile, tilts her head, and checks each of your pupils with her penlight, the way a first-aider checks whether someone is dead.
mechanics: SOURCE AND PIPELINE (checked, all reachable from this container): MakeHuman's hm08 base mesh and its morph targets have been CC0 since September 2020; the text is in every file header. raw.githubusercontent.com/makehumancommunity/makehuman/master/makehuman/data/... answers 200. A new offline tool, tools/matron_head/build_matron_head.py (numpy and Pillow only, run with python3 -I, no MakeHuman code used because that code is AGPL), downloads a pinned list of files by URL and SHA-256: 3dobjs/base.obj, the macro target universal-female-old-minmuscle-minweight, head/cheek/eyes/mouth/nose age targets, and expression units. It applies an age preset (head-age-incr 1.0, cheek-volume-decr 0.9-1.0, eye-bag-incr, eye-push1-in for sunken eyes, mouth-angles-down 0.6, nose-hump-incr 0.7 to keep today's hooked nose, mouth-laugh-lines-out 0.8, thinner lips). It cuts the head and neck from the 'body' group (4,250 quads, 4,274 vertices, 8,500 triangles) and keeps the helper-upper/lower-teeth, helper-tongue and eyelash groups. It repacks the head's UV islands, which are scattered over 21% of the full-body atlas, into their own 0..1 square. It writes one container, godot/presentation/life/matron_head/matron_head.bin, holding positions, normals, UVs, indices, sparse blend-shape deltas, neck bone weights and PNG blobs. Output is byte-identical between runs (seeded numpy PCG64).

BLEND SHAPES (MakeHuman expression units, CC0): blink_l and blink_r (eye-left/right-closure), lids_wide_l and lids_wide_r (eye-*-opened-up: the whites showing above the iris), jaw_open (mouth-open; it also moves all 68 lower-teeth vertices), lips_back (mouth-retraction), smile_l and smile_r (mouth-corner-puller, split by side), nostril_l and nostril_r (nose dilatation), neck_cords (neck-platysma), brow_inner_up. The tool also writes jaw_unhinged: the jaw region turned 0.6 rad and slid sideways, with smooth falloff weights, for the Turn's jaw_open values over 1.0. Found and proved here: in Godot 4.7 Compatibility, a code-built ArrayMesh in RELATIVE mode takes blend shapes as position deltas. Absolute positions double the mesh and push it out of frame.

NECK: a Skeleton3D with three bones (neck_lo, neck_hi, head) under the torso pivot, with weights baked by height between the collar ring and MakeHuman's joint-head (0.6975 m). Each frame, the existing neck.rotation and head.rotation from _pose() are split across the bones, so the Turn's 2.6 rad look back over her shoulder twists the neck over its length instead of spinning a rigid tube. MakeHuman's neck is 0.109 m from joint-neck to joint-head and today's NECK constant is 0.16, so neck_lo's rest length stretches to fit. That suits her long limbs, and a 10% extra stretch is added while she is PEERING.

SKIN SHADER (godot/presentation/life/matron_skin.gdshader, written for gl_compatibility, which both desktop and mobile use per project.godot). Inputs: albedo 1024 (age spots, capillary blush on the nose and cheeks, gray thin eyebrows painted in, a dark wet mouth interior chosen by geometry behind the lip line). A tangent-space normal map 1024, built from a baked height field: forehead lines, crow's feet radiating from the eye corners, smoker's lines around the lips, nasolabial folds, neck rings, all placed by region from 3D position and turned into normals by the UV gradient so Godot's MikkTSpace tangents match. A 256 tiling pore detail normal map. A masks texture: R distance from the source pocket (inverse-square falloff from the left breast pocket), G vein network, B thickness for ears, nose tip and eyelids, A cavity/occlusion. Compatibility has no subsurface scattering, so a custom light() function wraps diffuse light 0.45 past the terminator and adds a red-shifted scatter term weighted by thickness. Backlit ears glow red under the locker's work bulb.

EYES: a procedurally generated eyeball for each side, placed at MakeHuman's helper-eye centers (±0.0308, 0.7284, 0.1245 m, radius 0.015 m), each on its own pivot. matron_eye.gdshader draws a yellowed sclera with veins, a darker limbal ring, a parallax-offset iris (radial fiber noise), a pupil whose size is a uniform, a sharp corneal specular in light(), and a fake environment reflection (reflect() mapped to a cold sky and steel band). A darkening term under the upper lid, driven by blink weight and gaze pitch, keeps the eyes from looking like a doll's. A thin wet tear strip, generated along the lower lid's boundary loop with high specular, adds the wet line. The upper lid follows gaze pitch: blink weight +0.25 when she looks down.

GAZE: the eyes aim at the camera, clamped to ±35° yaw and ±25° pitch, and move in saccades (a 40 ms jump, then a 200-600 ms fixation) with 0.1-0.3° microsaccades. The eyes counter-rotate against her head roll, so even with the hunt's 1.35 rad head cock they stay on you. During a too-still window the microsaccades stop: a perfect, inhuman fixation.

WRONG BLINKING, by stage (from the 'stage' bridge key). Pest: about 15 a minute, 90 ms to close, 50 ms shut, 180 ms to open, both lids together. When sees_player turns on she stops blinking for 6-12 s, then gives one slow blink. Dangerous: slow blinks (300 ms to close, 400 ms shut) that close only 85%, leaving a sliver of white showing, plus occasional double blinks. Changed: the eyes blink out of step, one 80-150 ms ahead of the other, sometimes one eye alone, with eyelid twitching (10-20 Hz, 5% amplitude) between blinks. All of it is timed by the view's existing deterministic _hash() on clock beats, never randf.

MICRO-MOTION: a head tremor at 4-6 Hz, built from noise rather than a sine, growing from 0.2° to 0.6° with exposure, with a matching finger tremor added to the existing finger curls. Breathing at 14 breaths a minute, 26 when Changed: torso scale ±0.5%, nostril_l/r at 0.3 on the inhale, and jaw_open at 0.1 plus a flicker of neck_cords on labored breaths. Each breath's phase is reset when _update_figure() fires the existing matron_breath cue, so what you see matches the recorded breath you hear. Too-still windows set tremor, breathing and microsaccades to exactly zero for 1.5-4 s: on the sees_player edge within 15 m, while PEERING ('her breath held'), and still on her post (GUARDING at speed < 0.3).

MOUTH, synced to the audio cues that already exist: each matron_shriek cue in _update_figure() (sees, throws, leaps, climbs, Turn, fall) drives jaw_open 1.0, lips_back 0.8, neck_cords 1.0 and lids_wide 1.0 over 0.8 s. The Turn's jaw_open of 1.35 maps to jaw_open 1.0 plus jaw_unhinged 1.0, hanging to one side. As a pest she reads as an attendant: when she sees the player within 3 m, outside the Turn, she gives a polite smile that starts at one corner (smile_l 0.5, smile_r 0.15, with the right side lagging 120 ms) while her eyes do not smile (no lid squint), and tilts her head 0.25 rad in sympathy. The pest's shove lands in the middle of that smile.

TEETH, HAIR AND CAP: the teeth and tongue come from the MakeHuman helpers. The teeth shader gives yellowed enamel with translucent edges and one dark gap where a lower tooth is missing. The cap is generated, not modeled: scalp vertices above a hairline plane pushed 7 mm out along their normals, plus a folded brim, using the existing white dress material (_textured TUNIC_FRESH) so the tunic's exposure stains carry onto it. Thin gray hair is painted on the scalp under two alpha-scissor shells with the scalp showing through. Today's lank ribbon strands across the face (Body.ribbon) stay, re-rooted at the brim.

EXPOSURE (the 'exposure' key, 0..1 over kExposureFullSeconds = 600 s) follows the real stages of a radiation burn, restrained and never gore. Thresholds sweep across mask R (the pocket falloff) plus noise: redness, then dry peeling (flaky edges in the normal map), then a shiny weeping patch at the center (low roughness, yellowish), limited to 25% of the face's area while the neck may go further. Veins (mask G) show above 0.3 with a gray-violet tint. Petechiae (small dark-red dots) above 0.5. Hair loss: the painted hair mask thins in patches, the ribbon strands are hidden one by one, and above 0.6 a clump of hair shows on her tunic shoulder. Eyes: a blood patch on the white of the left eye above 0.6, a milky cornea that grows with exposure, and anisocoria (her left pupil 1.6 times the right) above 0.5. A thin red gum line shows when lips_back exposes it above 0.6. The same shader, in an object-space version with no UVs (like today's _textured), goes on her hands and forearms, worst on the right hand that picked the source up. _apply_exposure() keeps its SKIN_FRESH/BLISTERED/GREY tint as the base tone, so the body and face agree.

LIGHT THAT SHOWS HER FACE: her penlight. The _eye_light OmniLight3D is replaced by an unshadowed SpotLight3D (18°, 6 m, cold white) with a small penlight mesh. It is clipped to her left breast pocket (the same pocket that held the source), so its weak spill lights her chin from below. It is in her left hand, sweeping, while she PEERs and searches. If its cone hits the camera within 3 m, the player's screen whites out for 0.3 s. Her emergence is still lit by the locker's red alarm-lamp strobe (_lamp_light), which now falls on wet eyes and real skin.

THE PUPIL CHECK (the death beat): when the 'catches' key goes up (a kill by her hands while Changed), _feel_death() in main_feel.gd keeps the view in the corpse's eyes instead of pulling up and back. Her drawn torso and head lean in so her face is 0.4 m away. The penlight clicks on (a small synthesized click: machines make sounds) and goes to your left eye, then your right. Her head tilts, she smiles at one corner, blinks out of step, and the light clicks off before the respawn. It runs at most 3.2 s for her kills only (DEATH_CAM_MAX_S is 2.8 today), and a tap skips it, so it stays touch-only. The simulation is untouched: her capsule stays where the native puts it, and only the drawn pose and the camera change.

LOADING AND LEVEL OF DETAIL: the face loads its .bin at setup with FileAccess, builds the ArrayMesh, decodes the PNGs with Image.load_png_from_buffer, generates mipmaps and makes an ImageTexture. This is the same runtime-load pattern audio_director.gd _load_voice() uses with AudioStreamOggVorbis.load_from_file, so the CI runs, which never import, work unchanged. The old primitive head (Body.head(), about 35 draw calls of separate teeth, eyes, bags and ears) stays as the far version: visibility_range_end at 12 m on the new face, begin at 12 m on the old head, with hysteresis. godot/export_presets.cfg include_filter gains presentation/life/matron_head/*.

PHONE BUDGET: about 13k triangles for the whole new face (8.5k head, about 2k eyes, about 1k teeth and tongue, about 0.4k lashes, about 1.5k cap) in 8 draw calls, against about 35 for today's primitive head. Textures are uncompressed (no runtime ETC2 in export templates): albedo RGBA8 1024 with mipmaps 5.6 MB, normal RG8 2.8 MB, masks 512 1.4 MB, pores 0.35 MB, about 10 MB in all. The LOW quality preset (settings_store.gd QUALITY 0) halves them at load and drops the hair shells. Blend shapes and the 3-bone skin cost little (about 5k indexed vertices). The penlight casts no shadow. If memory gets tight, the upgrade path is VRAM-compressed ASTC through a CI step that runs godot --headless --import.

milestones.title: 1. Her real face (playable on its own)
milestones.what: Write tools/matron_head/build_matron_head.py: download the pinned CC0 files by SHA-256, apply the age preset, cut the head and neck, repack UVs, write blend-shape deltas and the 3-bone neck weights, and bake albedo, height-to-normal, masks and pores into godot/presentation/life/matron_head/matron_head.bin. Add godot/presentation/life/matron_face.gd (loader, ArrayMesh, Skeleton3D, generated eyeballs with matron_eye.gdshader, teeth, tongue, lashes, generated cap, the moved ribbon strands) and matron_skin.gdshader. In matron_view.gd, swap the head block of _build_figure() for the new face, split neck and head rotation across the bones, map jaw_open to the jaw blend shapes, aim the eyes at the camera with saccades, and give her normal blinks. The exposure tint follows the existing SKIN_* colors. The old primitive head becomes the version shown beyond 12 m. Add include_filter for the .bin and the MakeHuman CC0 notice on the licences page.
milestones.proof: New godot/tests/matron_face_test.gd (headless, --script) prints MATRON_FACE PASS lines: the .bin loads; the head has at most 6k vertices and the whole face at most 16k triangles; all named blend shapes and 3 bones are present; textures decode at the expected sizes; the face uses at most 10 draw surfaces; the eyes settle on a target within 1.5° within 0.3 s and stop at ±35°/±25°. milestones.title: 2. Alive, and wrong
milestones.what: In matron_face.gd, add the blink controller with its stage rules (the pest's stare on the sees_player edge, the Dangerous slow blinks that close only 85%, the Changed out-of-step blinks and eyelid twitching), the noise-built tremor that grows with exposure, breathing reset by the matron_breath cue (torso, nostrils, parted lips, neck cords), the too-still windows (the sees_player edge within 15 m, PEERING, GUARDING at rest), microsaccades that stop during stillness, eyes that counter-rotate against her head roll, mouth shapes fired by every matron_shriek cue, the Turn's jaw_unhinged shape, and the pest's one-sided professional smile with a head tilt within 3 m. Everything is timed by _hash() on clock beats.
milestones.proof: matron_face_test.gd gains cases on an injected clock. A pest that does not see the player for 60 s blinks 12-24 times, with both lids within 20 ms. On a sees_player edge at 8 m: no blinks and zero tremor for at least 1.5 s. Stage 1: closure peaks at most 0.85. Stage 2: at least 70% of blinks are out of step by at least 60 ms. A shriek cue brings jaw_open to at least 0.9 within 0.12 s. Within 3 m as a pest, smile_l is greater than smile_r. The gallery adds a 12-frame blink strip for each stage and a shriek frame.

milestones.title: 3. The source's work
milestones.what: Drive the exposure progression from the masks: redness, then peeling, then a shiny weeping patch spreading from the left breast pocket up the neck (capped at 25% of the face), veins above 0.3, petechiae above 0.5, patchy hair loss (painted hair mask, ribbon strands hidden one by one, a clump on her tunic shoulder above 0.6), a blood patch on the white of the left eye, a milky cornea, unequal pupils above 0.5, and a red gum line shown by lips_back. Put the object-space version of the skin shader on her hands and forearms, worst on the right hand, and add a pocket stain on the tunic.
milestones.proof: matron_face_test.gd checks the burn coverage computed on the CPU from the masks at each exposure threshold: 0% at exposure 0, rising steadily, at least 15% of neck texels at 1.0, at most 25% of face texels. Pupil ratio is 1.0 below 0.5 and 1.6 at 1.0. Uniforms only ever rise with exposure. The gallery renders a series at exposure 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0 at 0.45 m under the locker's work bulb and the penlight. In touch_matron_act (about 380 s of play, so exposure about 0.6) the stage screenshots show the burn on her neck.

milestones.title: 4. The pupil check, and the phone pass
milestones.what: Replace _eye_light with the penlight SpotLight3D and mesh (clipped to the pocket, in her hand while PEERING or searching, a 0.3 s screen whiteout when its cone hits the camera within 3 m). Add the death beat in main_feel.gd when 'catches' goes up: the view stays in the corpse's eyes, she leans in, the light goes to each eye, she tilts her head, smiles at one corner, blinks out of step, the light clicks off. At most 3.2 s, a tap skips it. Then the phone pass: LOW quality halves the textures and drops the hair shells, visibility ranges are tuned, and the APK is checked for the .bin.
milestones.proof: touch_matron_act asserts that matron_view.pupil_checks goes up after her kill, that the respawn still comes within 3.5 s, and that a tap ends the beat early. --capture writes the pupil-check frames. A gallery scenario checks RenderingServer.get_rendering_info primitives (at most 16k more) and draw calls (at most 10 more for the face) with her at 0.45 m. The CI's APK step checks with unzip -l that presentation/life/matron_head/matron_head.bin is in the APK. Under law 31, frame times on the owner's Fold from the CI APK are the only proof of phone performance, and this desktop check stands in until then.

risks: Mannequin instead of uncanny: the MakeHuman base is a clean, generic 'CG human'. Realism has to come from the baked albedo (blotches, capillaries, age spots), the wet eyes, the wrinkle normals and the micro-motion. Mitigation: the owner reviews the gallery's 0.45 m close-ups at every milestone, and the age preset and texture fields are numbers in the tool, quick to retune and rebake.

Compatibility renderer limits: no SSS, SSAO, SSR or refraction. Translucency, eye occlusion and reflections are all faked. The renders were made on llvmpipe, which can differ from the Fold's Adreno GPU, so the CI APK must be checked on the device (law 31).

Raw runtime files and export: the .bin is not a Godot resource, so it ships only if godot/export_presets.cfg include_filter lists it. The APK unzip -l check guards this. Do not give it a .png or .glb name that the importer would take over.

Memory: about 10 MB of uncompressed textures, because export templates cannot compress ETC2 at runtime. LOW quality halves it. If that is not enough, add a godot --headless --import CI step and move to imported ASTC textures, a change that reaches all 61 existing .import files.

Normal-map tangents: normals come from the height field's UV gradient and are read with Godot's MikkTSpace tangents. Seams can show lighting steps, so pad the islands and place seams under the cap, behind the ears and under the jaw.

Neck twist: 2.6 rad shared by three linear-blend-skinned bones will lose some volume (the candy-wrapper effect). The collar and the stretch help, but the Turn's look back over her shoulder may need its own twist split or a limit.

Taste: radiation burns can drift into gore. The rules are in the numbers: face burn coverage at most 25%, no open wounds, blood only at the gum line and in one eye, and the horror kept in small, plausible details.
The death beat delays the retry: at most 3.2 s, skippable by tap, and only after her kills. The test asserts the respawn time.
Licensing hygiene: copy no MakeHuman Python (AGPL), only CC0 data. Record each file's URL and SHA-256 in the tool, and add the notice on the licences page even though CC0 does not require it.

Blend-shape pitfall found while prototyping: code-built shapes in RELATIVE mode take deltas. matron_face_test.gd should assert the face's bounding box is unchanged with every weight at 1.0, so a wrong encoding can never ship.

The bake tool is the biggest single piece of work (UV repack, a numpy rasterizer that maps texels to 3D positions, the wrinkle and burn fields). If it slips, milestone 1 can ship with only albedo tint, cavity and pores, and add the wrinkles in milestone 3.
design:face:3.wow: You die under her hands and the screen does not cut away. You are lying in your own dead eyes, looking up. She leans in until her face fills the view, close enough to see her pores, the peeling skin climbing her neck from her breast pocket, and one pupil wider than the other. Her penlight clicks on and goes to your left eye, then your right. She tilts her head, the corner of her mouth lifts in a polite little smile, she blinks one eye a beat after the other, and the light clicks off.
